name: triton_fp8_permute_lds_tile
description: PyTorch's generic `.permute(...).contiguous()` for 1-byte dtypes (fp8/uint8) runs at ~12% of HBM peak. An LDS-tile Triton transpose kernel hits ~85% peak. For 377 MB fp8 permute on gfx950: 1534 µs → 168 µs = 9.2× speedup. Critical for any HIP kernel that needs to rearrange fp8 operand layouts between Triton quant output and HIP kernel input (e.g., wgrad col-quant → HIP fwd-reuse).
preconditions: Need a byte-level transpose / permute of a fp8 (or uint8) tensor
Source tensor stored [M, N] row-major, want [G, N, M_g] contig output (or similar transpose)
steps: Write a Triton kernel with BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64 tile (16 KB LDS per tile — comfortable)
Load source tile coalesced: src + rm[:, None] * stride_m + rn[None, :] (thread row varies slower, col faster)
Store transposed: dst + rn[:, None] * stride_m_out + rm[None, :] via tl.trans(tile)
Use num_warps=4 for gfx950; Triton's BlockedLayout picks sensible thread mapping when rows × cols both ≥ 64
View fp8 as uint8 for the kernel (they have same byte layout); view back at end
Grid: (cdiv(M_g, BLOCK_M), cdiv(N, BLOCK_N), G) for per-group transpose
expected_impact: 377 MB fp8: 1534 us → 168 us (9.2× speedup). Enables HIP wgrad path that was 0.44× Triton to reach 0.99× Triton kernel-only. Reference impl: `Primus-Turbo/primus_turbo/hip/grouped_gemm_mxfp8/_permute_fp8.py::fp8_permute_M_to_GN`.
decision_rules: ALWAYS profile before assuming the kernel is the bottleneck. In the HIP wgrad case, 60% of time was in a torch API call running at 1/10th of HBM peak.
Use for any fp8/uint8 / int8 permute. bf16 permute via torch is less bad (~30% HBM peak) but still benefits from this pattern.
Don't try to pre-fuse the permute into an upstream quant kernel without measuring — Triton's blocked layout may fight the permuted store (see skill `triton_permuted_store_blocking_layout_pitfall`).
